name: Karaitirunathar (Sathyanatheswarar) Temple, Kanchipuram
deity: Shiva as Karaitirunathar (Sathyanatheswarar, Karaivananathar), a self-manifested lingam, with the Goddess Pramarambikai
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thondai Nadu, sung in the Tevaram by Sambandar (7th century)
summary: At Thirukalimedu in Kanchipuram, the self-manifested Sathyanatheswarar of the old karai-tree forest is remembered as the Lord before whom Indra sought release from a sage's curse, and whom Sambandar sang.

sections.history: Kachi Nerikaraikadu, today the Sathyanatheswarar temple at Thirukalimedu on the eastern side of Kanchipuram, is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams and a Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thondai Nadu, counted fifth among the shrines of that country. Thirugnana Sambandar sang its Lord in a pathigam of the Tevaram, which places it among the sacred sites of the seventh century. The old name recalls the karai trees whose thicket once covered the place, and the Lord is still called Karaitirunathar or Karaivananathar, the Lord of the karai forest; old inscriptions are said to record the shrine as Thiru Neri Karaikadu. The temple stands near the Indra Theertham, the tank tied to its chief legend.
sections.architecture: The temple is a modest Dravidian shrine in a walled court. The east-facing central sanctum holds Sathyanatheswarar, a lingam revered as self-manifested, and the goddess Pramarambikai has her own shrine facing south, where her festival image is kept. The tank outside, the Indra Theertham, completes the setting and gives the shrine its link with the king of the gods.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Indra, cursed by the sage Gautama for his wrong against Ahalya, came to this karai forest and did penance before the Lord to recover his lost form, bathing in the tank that bears his name. Tradition adds that Budhan, the planet Mercury, also worshipped Shiva here, and devotees troubled by Mercury in their horoscopes come to pray at this shrine.
sections.festivals: Margazhi Thiruvadhirai, Maha Shivaratri and the Annabhishekam of Aippasi, when the lingam is covered with cooked rice, are the main observances, together with Pradosham each fortnight. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thirukalimedu lies on the eastern edge of Kanchipuram, away from the crowded temple streets, and the shrine keeps a village calm. Pilgrims come to the self-manifested Lord and his tank, and many offer prayers for Budhan. It combines well with the Vishnu shrines of eastern Kanchipuram and with the Ekambareswarar and Kamakshi temples in the centre.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most neighbourhood temples of Kanchipuram. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer areas, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is in Thirukalimedu, on the eastern side of Kanchipuram near the Indra Theertham, a short auto ride from the Kanchipuram bus stand and railway station. Kanchipuram is linked by road to Chennai, Chengalpattu, Vellore and Arakkonam; Chennai International Airport, roughly 70 km away, is the nearest airport.
